Perplexity is looking for a Design Engineer to help turn perplexity.com http://perplexity.com into a real growth engine, not a pile of one-off pages. You'll sit shoulder to shoulder with brand designers, PMMs, growth, and content teams, shipping product launch pages, campaign landing pages, and the components and tooling that let those teams move fast without lowering the bar.

This is a hands-on role for someone with real taste, sharp attention to detail, and the speed to turn a Figma file, a Slack thread, or a rough sketch into a polished, shipped page quickly.

Tech stack: React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Sanity



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Ship product launch pages and evergreen marketing pages for products like Comet, Computer, Deep Research, Search, and Hub. Own the work from Figma handoff to production.

 - Partner with brand designers to build interactive experiences that make the site feel alive and drive engagement.

 - Maintain and extend our brand design system and component library, keeping Figma and production in sync so brand and creative can scaffold pages with guardrails.

 - Work closely with the paid ads and growth teams to run A/B tests on landing pages, popups, and upsell modules. Read the results, then iterate.

 - Migrate the leftover Framer collections to Sanity, model schemas that non-engineers can actually use, and help ship new content types like changelog, customer stories, and academy pages.

 - Design and unblock yourself when design resources are constrained. You can take a rough direction and turn it into something worth shipping.

 - Improve the tools around the work: CMS workflows, i18n, SEO, experimentation, and internal tooling for marketing self-serve. If a manual process is slowing the team down, you should want to fix it.


WHAT YOU NEED

 - 3+ years of experience as a front-end or design engineer, ideally on a marketing or growth site.

 - A portfolio site that shows your previous work on marketing sites and design work.

 - Strong skills in React, CSS, and modern frameworks.

 - Deep understanding of responsive design and design-to-code workflows. You know what the platform can do and you stay current on what's new.

 - Experience maintaining a reusable component library and sweating the design details in code.

 - A real eye for design. You can tell the difference between "almost right" and "actually right," and your work reflects it.

 - Attention to detail that shows up unprompted. The 2px misalignment, the wrong easing curve, the widow at the end of the paragraph.

 - Stellar communication skills and a track record of working effectively in cross-functional teams. You can defend a decision, push back constructively, and explain trade-offs to non-technical stakeholders.

 - Desire to work in a fast-paced environment, continuously grow, and master your craft.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience running A/B tests and reading experiments results in a growth context.

 - Knowledge of SEO principles, structured data, and localization workflows.

 - Experience with web animations (GSAP, Motion, Web Animations API), 3D libraries, or interactive storytelling.

 - Experience working with a headless CMS (Sanity, Contentful).

 - Experience building internal tools or AI-assisted workflows that made a marketing or design team faster.

About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. The Identity team builds the foundational systems that enable people, organizations, devices, and agents to securely access OpenAI products.

The team works across consumer and enterprise experiences, including account structures, sign-in, authentication, recovery, privacy, permissions, administration, and agent identity. As AI systems become increasingly capable of acting on behalf of people and organizations, we are defining new models for authorization and trust across human-to-agent and agent-to-agent interactions.

About the Role

In this role, you’ll lead design for foundational identity experiences across OpenAI’s products. You’ll make permissions, access, risk, and administration feel clear, safe, and genuinely usable—whether someone is securing a personal account, administering access across an enterprise, signing in to another product with ChatGPT, or authorizing an agent to perform sensitive work.

Your work will span established identity challenges and emerging interaction models without established design conventions. You’ll help define how users understand what an agent can access, who or what it is acting on behalf of, and when confirmation or stronger authentication should appear. Working closely with product, engineering, security, privacy, and design, you’ll translate complex policies and technical systems into coherent, trustworthy experiences.

This role is based in our San Francisco HQ. We offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Lead the design direction for identity, account security, permissions, and administrative experiences across OpenAI’s consumer and enterprise products.

 - Design and ship high-quality experiences spanning sign-in, authentication, account recovery, device accounts, privacy, access controls, governance, and remediation.

 - Define mental models and interaction patterns for human-to-agent and agent-to-agent identity, authorization, and trust.

 - Help users understand what people, systems, and agents can access or do on their behalf.

 - Design security checks and confirmation flows that protect sensitive actions while minimizing unnecessary friction.

 - Partner closely with product management, engineering, security, privacy, and design peers to shape strategy, roadmap, and execution.

 - Navigate complex roles, policies, dependencies, and product states to create systems that remain coherent as they scale.

 - Contribute to and evolve the design systems and patterns used across OpenAI’s identity experiences.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Are a systems-oriented product thinker who can reason across complex states, dependencies, policies, and user types.

 - Have designed role-based access or permissions for organizations with multiple teams, resources, or levels of administration.

 - Understand how to balance security, usability, and business needs in high-stakes workflows.

 - Have strong UX/UI and interaction design skills, with a high bar for contemporary craft, clarity, and quality.

 - Can turn complicated technical capabilities and policies into mental models that users can understand and trust.

 - Are comfortable shaping direction when both the underlying technology and established user expectations are evolving.

 - Have experience with enterprise, platform, desktop, infrastructure, or similarly complex product environments.

 - Are excited to establish new conventions for identity and access in a world where AI agents increasingly act on behalf of people and organizations.
